page: Microsoft Azure D96pds_v6 is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the ARM64 architecture using Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processors under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 96 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.4 GHz, operating with one thread per core to ensure unshared execution resources per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 64 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, alongside a shared 128 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 384 GB, delivering 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture features a bundled 5,670 GB local NVMe SSD, while GPU acceleration is not present.

Benchmark data reflects strong parallel compute and memory subsystems. The platform secures top-tier classifications in multi-core metrics, including stress-ng multi-core CPU testing at 198,272.95 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 845.76 GB/sec. Memory throughput reaches 464.68 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 205.46 GB/sec for write operations. Application benchmarks align with these results, yielding top-tier performance in Redis SET operations at 170.16 million operations per second, static web serving throughput at 102.57 GB/sec, Clang compilation, and database operations. Single-threaded performance benchmarks in the average tier across Geekbench and stress-ng tests, indicating that processing velocity relies on core concurrency rather than peak single-thread frequency.

The server presents distinct hardware tradeoffs rooted in its ARM processor design. The lack of x86 vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX shifts suitability away from legacy x86 instruction sets and dense matrix calculations, though cryptographic acceleration via AES is supported. The high core density paired with large internal NVMe storage provides favorable infrastructure efficiency for scale-out architectures by consolidating massive multi-threaded tasks into a single virtual host. Consequently, the instance is well suited for high-throughput distributed database nodes, parallel software build pipelines, web serving fleets, and large memory-bound data processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D96pds_v6 is an ARM-based general-purpose virtual machine designed for high-concurrency cloud workloads. Powered by 96 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 physical cores operating at 3.4 GHz with single-threaded cores, the instance pairs compute density with 384 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. A bundled 5,670 GB NVMe SSD provides expansive high-throughput local storage, while the architecture omits dedicated GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates exceptional multi-threaded performance, reaching top-tier results in Clang software compilation, Redis key-value operations, static web throughput, and uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 460 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core execution metrics sit in the average bracket, highlighting a profile optimized for parallel scale rather than serial instruction latency. By leveraging efficient ARM silicon and high resource density, the instance offers strong cost efficiency for parallelized processing. It is best suited for large database deployments, intensive CI/CD build farms, and web-scale serving.
